title: Two Views of the Same Data
subtitle: Combining bar charts and scatter plots to tell a richer story

introduction.value: This story demonstrates how to combine **multiple scrolly sections** with text interludes. Each section uses a different visualization to explore the same dataset from a new angle.
The pattern is simple: text content lives in `copy.json`, components live in Svelte. No string-to-component mapping needed.

barSteps.value: We start with four categories. Each bar shows a **count** value.
**Category B** stands out as the tallest — it has a count of 50.
But **Category A** is interesting too. Its count is 30, but it has a much higher *rate*.
Let's zoom the Y-axis to see the differences more clearly.

interlude.value: Bars are great for comparing magnitudes, but they only show one dimension. What if each category also has a **rate** — a second variable that tells a different story?
The slope chart above shows the disconnect: **B** dominates in count but drops in rate, while **A** does the opposite. A scatter plot lets us see both dimensions at once.

scatterSteps.value: Now each category is a point. The **x-axis** shows count, the **y-axis** shows rate.
Category A has a **high rate but low count** — top-left. Category B has a **high count but low rate** — bottom-right.
The dashed line shows the **average rate**. Two categories sit above it, two below.

conclusion.value: By using two visualizations in sequence, we revealed something a single chart couldn't: **count and rate tell different stories**. Category B *looks* dominant in the bar chart, but Category A has the highest rate.
This multi-section pattern — text, scrolly, text, scrolly, text — lets you build layered narratives without cramming everything into one view.
